title: Rocket Report: Starship set for historic test flight; a century of Electron
gist: This Rocket Report shows a US launch capacity crunch as SpaceX winds down Falcon and its Transporter rideshare: Rocket Lab raised Neutron's price from $55M to $70M, and the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital lent $150M each to Stoke Space and Rocket Lab. Starship Flight 15 is attempting the first full recovery of an orbital launch system, and SpaceX now calls itself an infrastructure company accelerated by AI.

themes.theme: US launch capacity crunch and pricing power

insights.claim: Rocket Lab raised the price of a dedicated Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million, citing strong customer demand and a constrained launch market, and says bookings continue.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A 27% price hike that doesn't deter bookings signals real pricing power for medium-lift entrants.

insights.claim: The coming shortage of US launch capacity, driven mainly by SpaceX sunsetting its Transporter rideshare program, has sparked a flurry of interest in new medium-lift rockets.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: SpaceX's retreat from rideshare opens share for competitors such as Rocket Lab, Stoke, and Firefly.

insights.claim: Customers' next available slots on Rocket Lab's Neutron are now in the 2030s and beyond.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Backlog extending into the 2030s supports revenue visibility but also shows capacity is scarce.
insights.quote: Customers’ next options to fly on Neutron are now in the 2030s and beyond.

insights.claim: The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital is propping up SpaceX competitors because defense officials appear to see the retirement of the Falcon rocket as a potential national security risk.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Government capital backstops launch competitors, lowering financing risk for the sector.
insights.locator: The launch crunch comes to national security.

insights.claim: The Office of Strategic Capital made a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Stoke Space for a second launch pad at Cape Canaveral and a second $150 million loan to Rocket Lab to raise Neutron's flight rate.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Non-dilutive government debt accelerates capacity build-out for both companies.

insights.claim: Rocket Lab's Electron was set to fly its 100th mission on November 14, carrying an iQPS synthetic aperture radar satellite; Electron first flew in 2017.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: 100 flights validates Electron as a durable commercial franchise.

insights.claim: Eric Berger credits Rocket Lab as the world's second purely commercial launch business to succeed.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Positions Rocket Lab as the clear number-two commercial launcher behind SpaceX.

insights.claim: Firefly Aerospace signed a deal with Japanese SAR operator Synspective for up to 10 Alpha launches through 2030, each carrying two satellites for up to 20 total, using Alpha's 1,000 kg LEO capacity.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Adds multi-year backlog to Firefly's small-launch business.

insights.claim: Stoke Space signed a multi-launch agreement with Planet Labs, with undisclosed numbers and pricing, that may be open-ended given Planet's steady need to replenish its Earth-imaging fleet.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Constellation-replenishment demand creates recurring revenue for new launchers.
insights.locator: Stoke and Planet sign multi-launch agreement.

insights.claim: SAR constellation operators (iQPS, Synspective) are a recurring source of launch demand across multiple small launchers.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Growth of SAR Earth-observation constellations underpins small-launch demand.

insights.claim: Avio's plan to raise Vega C cadence to six, then nine flights per year needs more investment, and raises the question of whether that is a good use of resources when emerging European launchers may offer comparable capacity.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Signals strategic risk to Avio's Vega franchise from new European entrants.
insights.locator: Is the Vega rocket a dead end?

insights.claim: A single Ariane 64 launch requires the equivalent of a full year of Vega C solid rocket boosters at its baseline cadence of four flights, so the two vehicles compete for constrained booster production.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Solid-booster production is a bottleneck that caps European launch growth.
insights.quote: a single Ariane 64 launch requires the equivalent of an entire year’s worth of solid rocket boosters for Vega C
insights.locator: Boosters may be better used by Ariane 6 …

themes.theme: New rocket programs: skepticism on timelines

insights.claim: AST SpaceMobile CEO Abel Avellan plans a 'simple' Blacklift rocket with 20 metric tons of lift, a reusable first stage, and twice-monthly launches from Wallops, tailored to carry five Bluebird satellites at a time; Berger calls this a little naive.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Vertical integration into launch is a major execution and capital risk for AST SpaceMobile.
insights.quote: you can simplify it as a big tank feeding engines

insights.claim: Firefly CEO Jason Kim would not commit to a 2027 launch of the Eclipse rocket co-developed with Northrop Grumman, despite over 175 Miranda engine hot fires; Berger concludes Eclipse won't be on a pad any time soon.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Expect Eclipse timeline slippage; medium-lift revenue for Firefly is further out.
insights.quote: Bottom line: Don’t expect to see Eclipse on a launch pad any time soon.

themes.theme: Starship full reuse and SpaceX's AI/infrastructure pivot

insights.claim: Starship Flight 15 aims to return both Super Heavy and the Starship upper stage to the launch site for catch, which would be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Full reuse would sharply cut SpaceX's marginal launch cost and widen its moat.
insights.quote: If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system.
insights.locator: Starship set for 15th test flight on Friday.

insights.claim: The Flight 15 Starship will deliver 26 Starlink V3 satellites, complete about 14 orbits at roughly 275 km over more than 22 hours, and attempt the upper stage landing the next day.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Starship carrying operational Starlink V3 payloads shows a move from testing to revenue missions.

insights.claim: SpaceX VP of launch Kiko Dontchev said SpaceX is fundamentally an infrastructure company building on the ground, in LEO, and soon on the Moon, and that the company has pivoted to data and AI over the last 18 months.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: SpaceX's value increasingly rests on Starlink/data/AI infrastructure rather than launch alone.
insights.quote: we are a rocket company, but fundamentally we are an infrastructure company at this point

insights.claim: Dontchev said AI is critical to accelerating SpaceX's pace of innovation and will get the company to Mars much faster.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: AI adoption inside aerospace engineering is framed as a speed advantage.
insights.quote: We’re going to get there so much faster.
